question: What bounded conditional H0 likelihood minima do flat LCDM and one explicitly fixed constant-w extension produce for the full DESI DR2 Gaussian BAO compression?
base_parameters: ../lcdm-reference/reference.json:parameters; same physical densities, 0.06 eV thermal relic, recombination, primordial and reionization state

constant-w.Omega_fld: omitted so CLASS infers fluid density from closure
constant-w.interpretation: A chosen constant-w subclass of source-defined CPL, not a paper best fit or native alternative qualification

fit.conditioned_coordinates: All other base physical, species, nuisance and alternative-fluid coordinates fixed
fit.target: DESI DR2 released full13 fitted BAO compression with full13 covariance
fit.ruler: Same evaluated CLASS state's predicted thermal drag horizon; no supplied drag redshift
fit.native_gaussian: Existing reviewed lcdm-bao-reference consumer, one arbitrary mean under anchor transport per process
fit.optimizer: Uniform grid, adjacent interior bracket, deterministic golden-section minimization; finite-resolution conditional result

optional_separate_planck_score.prior: Separate relative calibration penalty at fixed A_planck=1

qualification_limits: These are conditional fits to released fitted distance summaries, not fits to original galaxy observations.
Finite optimizer brackets do not prove a global minimum or define an uncertainty interval.
Emitted CLASS table interpolation and source-supplied precision have no certified error bound here.
Each full-output final prediction is rescored; its difference from the background-only fit policy is recorded explicitly.
CMB, BAO, SN and overlapping SH0ES summaries are never multiplied into a joint target by this workflow.
Original SN covariance refusal and separately named symmetric working profile remain unchanged.
Unit-test synthetic controls are excluded from observed data and reported scores.
CLASS external-reference execution does not establish native Irreducible CMB or constant-w physics.
